detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Calculus
detailed_solution.markdown:

detailed_solution.markdown:

Removing radicals we get,

at the centre of the plank is

detailed_solution.concept: Solid Mechanics - Shear Force and Bending Moment
detailed_solution.markdown: The plank will be balanced by the buoyant force acting under its bottom. Let the intensity of buoyant force be w. $$\begin{aligned} \text{For equilibrium, }w \times L&=W+W \\ \Rightarrow \quad w&=\frac{2 W}{L}\text{ upwards}\\ \end{aligned}$$ Thus, the bending moment at the centre of the plank will be $$\begin{aligned} M &=\frac{2 W}{L} \times \frac{L}{2} \times \frac{L}{4}-W \times \frac{L}{4} \\ \Rightarrow \quad M&=\frac{W L}{4}-\frac{W L}{4}=0 \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

In a compaction test, G, w, S and e represent the specific gravity, water content,

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Compaction of Soil
detailed_solution.markdown:
The bulk unit weight of soil is given by

$\gamma=\frac{(G+S e) \gamma_{w}}{1+e}$

For dry unit weight, degree of saturation,

$S=0 \quad \therefore \gamma_{d}=\frac{G \gamma_{w}}{1+e}$

$G w=\text { Se } \quad \therefore \gamma_{d}=\frac{G \gamma_{w}}{1+\frac{G w}{S}}$

For zero air voids, degree of saturation,

$S=100 \% \quad \therefore \gamma_{d}=\frac{G \gamma_{w}}{1+G w}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2010:q25.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 25
ce:2010:q25.question: The local mean time at a place located in longitude 90$^{\circ}$40' E when the standard time is 6 hours and 30 minutes and the standard meridian is 82$^{\circ}$30' E is

detailed_solution.concept: Geomatics Engineering - Theodolites, Compass and Traverse Surveying
detailed_solution.markdown:
Difference between standard meridian and the longitude of the given

$\text { place }=90^{\circ} 40^{\circ} \mathrm{E}-82^{\circ} 30^{\circ} \mathrm{E}=8^{\circ} 10^{\prime}$

The longitude of the given place is more than the standard meridian. Hence the local mean time of the given place will be ahead of the standard time.

$8^{\circ}=\frac{8}{15} \text { hours }$

=0 hours and 32 minutes and 0 seconds

$10^{\prime}=\frac{10}{15} \text { minutes }$

=0 hours and 0 minutes and 40 seconds

Time for a difference of $8^{\circ} 10^{\prime}=32$ minutes and 40 seconds

Local mean time = standard time +32 minutes and 40 seconds

$$\begin{aligned} =& 6 \text { hours and } 30 \text { minutes } \\ &+32 \text { minutes and } 40 \text { seconds } \\ =& 7 \text { hours, } 02 \text { minutes and } 40 \text{seconds} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2010:q30.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 30
ce:2010:q30.question:
A parabolic cable is held between two supports at the same level. The horizontal
span between the supports is L. The sag at the mid-span is h. The equation of
the parabola is $y=4h\frac{x^{2}}{L^{2}}$, where x is the horizontal coordinate and y is the vertical coordinate with the origin at the center of the cable. The expression for the total length of the cable is

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Ordinary Differential Equation
detailed_solution.markdown:
Length of curve $f(x)$ between $x=a$ and $x=b$ is given by,

$\int_{a}^{b}\sqrt{1+\left ( \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x} \right )^{2}}dx$

$$\begin{aligned}   y&=4h\frac{x^{2}}{L^{2}}   \;\; ...(i) \\    \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}&=8h\frac{x}{L^{2}} \end{aligned}$$

since, $y=0$ at $x=0$

and $y=h$ at $x=\frac{L}{2}$

(As can be seen from equation (i), by substituting $x=0$ and $x=\frac{L}{2}$)

$\therefore \;\; \frac{1}{2}$ (Length of cable) $=\int_{0}^{L/2}\sqrt{1+\left ( \frac{8hx}{L^{2}} \right )^{2}}dx$

Length of cable $=2\int_{0}^{L/2}\sqrt{1+64\frac{h^{2}x^{2}}{L^{4}}}dx$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2010:q31.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 31
ce:2010:q31.question:
Given a function
$f(x,y) = 4x^{2}+6y^{2}- 8x - 4y + 8.$
The optimal value of f(x,y)

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Calculus
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} f\left ( x, y \right )&=4x^{2}+6y^{2}-8x-4y+8 \\ \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}&=8x-8 \\ \frac{\partial f}{\partial y}&=12y-4y \\ \text{Putting, } \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}&=0 \\ \text{and } \frac{\partial f}{\partial y} =0 \\ 8x-8&=0 \\ \text{and }12y-4y&=0\\ \text{Given, } x&=1 \text{ and }y=\frac{1}{3} \\ \left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )& \text{ is the only stationary point.}\\  r&=\left [ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2} \right ]_{\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )}=8 \\   s&=\left [ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial xdy} \right ]_{\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )}=0 \\   t&=\left [ \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial y^2} \right ]_{\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )}=12 \\ \text{Since, } rt&=8\times 12=48 \\  s^{2}&=0\\ \text{Since, }rt \gt s^{2},\end{aligned}$$

we have either a maxima or minima at $\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )$

also since, $r=\left [ \frac{\partial f}{\partial x^2} \right ]_{1,\, \frac{1}{3}}=8 \gt 0$, the point $\left ( 1,\, \frac{1}{3} \right )$ is a point of minima.

The minimum value is,

$f\left ( 1,\frac{1}{3} \right )=4\times 1^{2}+6\times \frac{1}{3^{2}-8\times 1-4\times \frac{1}{3}+8} =\frac{10}{3}$

So the optimal value of f(x, y) is a minimum equal to $\frac{10}{3}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2010:q32.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 32
ce:2010:q32.question: A double cover butt riveted joint is used to connect two flat of 200 mm width and 14 mm thickness as shown in the figure. Strength of the riveted joint in double shear

$=12\times 72.61=871.32 kN$

Strength of one rivet in bearing $={d}'t\times \sigma _{b} =\left ( 20+1.5 \right )\times 14\times 300\times 10^{-3}=90.3 kN$

Strength of the riveted joint in bearing

$=12\times 90.3=1083.6 kN$

Thus the strength of joint will be governed by shearing and it will be equal to 871.32 kN

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2010:q33.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 33

detailed_solution.markdown:
As per Boussinesq equation, the vertical stress $\sigma_{2}$ at a point located at a depth 'z' and a horizontal distance 'r' from the point of application of point load Q is

$\sigma_{z}=\frac{3 Q}{2 \pi z^{2}}\left[\frac{1}{1+\left(\frac{r}{z}\right)^{2}}\right]^{5 / 2}$

For a horizontal distance $\frac{r}{2}$ and a depth $\frac{2}{2}$, the stress will be

$=\frac{3 Q}{2 \pi\left(\frac{z}{2}\right)^{2}}\left[\frac{1}{1+\left(\frac{r / 2}{2 / 2}\right)^{2}}\right]^{5 / 2}=4 \times \frac{3 Q}{2 \pi z^{2}}\left(\frac{1}{1+\left(\frac{r}{z}\right)^{2}}\right)^{5 / 2}$

$=4 \sigma_{z}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2010:q38.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 38
ce:2010:q38.question:
An open ended steel barrel of 1m height and 1m diameter is filled with saturated
fine sand having coefficient of permability of $10^{-2}$ m/s. The barrel stands on a saturated bed of gravel. The time required for the water level in the barrel to drop by 0.75m is

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Effective Stress and Permeability
detailed_solution.markdown:

ce:2010:q39.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 39
ce:2010:q39.question:
The ultimate load capacity of a 10 m long concrete pile of square cross section
500mm x 500 mm driven into a homogeneous clay layer having undrained cohesion
value of 40 kPa is 700 kN. If the cross section of the pile is reduced to 250mm x 2500 mm
and the length of the pile is increased to 20 m, the ultimate load capacity will be

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Deep Foundation
detailed_solution.markdown:
The ultimate load of a pile in clay is given by,

$$\begin{aligned} Q_{u}=& c N A_{b}+\alpha c A_{s} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 700=& 40 \times 9 \times 0.5 \times 0.5+\alpha \times 40 \\ & \times 0.5 \times 4 \times 10 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \alpha&=0.7625 \\ \text { Again, } \quad Q_{u}=& 40 \times 9 \times 0.25 \times 0.25+0.7625 \times 40 \\ & \times 0.25 \times 4 \times 20 \\ Q_{u} &=632.5 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2010:q40.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 40
ce:2010:q40.question:
For a rectangular channel seetion, Group I lists geometrical elements and Group II gives proportions for hydraulically efficient section

$y_e$ is the flow depth corresponding to hydraulically efficient section. The correct match of Group I with Group II is

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Open Channel Flow
detailed_solution.markdown:
Let the width of rectangular channel be B and depth of flow be y.

Area of flow, A=By

Wetted perimeter,

$P=B+2 y=\frac{A}{y}+2 y$

For hydraulically most efficient section, P should be minimum.

$$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \frac{d P}{d y}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{-A}{y^{2}}+2&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad A_{\theta}&=2 y_{e}^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad B_{e} y_{e}&=2 y_{\theta}^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad B_{\theta}&=2 y_{e} \end{aligned}$$

Hydraulic radius,

$R=\frac{A}{P}=\frac{2 y_{e}^{2}}{2 y_{e}+2 y_{e}}=\frac{y_{e}}{2}$

Top width,

$T=B=2 y_{e}$

Perimeter,

$P=B+2 y_{e}=2 y_{e}+2 y_{e}=4 y_{e}$

Hydraulic depth,

$D=\frac{A}{T}=\frac{2 y_{e}^{2}}{2 y_{e}}=y_{e}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ce:2010:q41.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 41
ce:2010:q41.question:
The Froude number of flow in a rectangular channel is 0.8. If te depth of flow is
1.5m, the critical depth is

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Open Channel Flow
detailed_solution.markdown:
Froude Number for a rectangular channel is given by

$$\begin{aligned} F &=\frac{V}{\sqrt{g y}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad V &=0.8 \times \sqrt{9.81 \times 1.5} \\ &=3.07 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ Discharge per unit width of rectangular channel is given by

$q=V y=3.07 \times 1.5=4.6 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{s} / \mathrm{m}$

$\therefore$ Critical depth,

$y_{c}=\left(\frac{q^{2}}{g}\right)^{1 / 3}=\left(\frac{4.6^{2}}{9.81}\right)^{1 / 3}=1.29 m$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2010:q42.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 42
ce:2010:q42.question:
A well of diameter 20 cm fully penetrates a confined aquifer. After a long period
of pumping at rate of 2720 litres per minute, the observations of drawdown taken
at 10 m and 100 m distances from the centre of the well are found to be 3m and
0.5m respectively. The transmissivity of the aquifer is

primary.subtopicLabel: Source of Water Supply, Distribution System and Well Hydraulics

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Source of Water Supply, Distribution System and Well Hydraulics
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} Q &=\frac{2 \pi T\left(s_{1}-s_{2}\right)}{\ln \left(\frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}}\right)} \\ T &=\frac{2720 \times 10^{-3} \times 24 \times 60 \times \ln \left(\frac{100}{10}\right)}{2 \times \pi \times(3-0.5)} \\ &=574.26 \mathrm{m}^{2} / \mathrm{day} \simeq 576 \mathrm{m}^{2} / \mathrm{day} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2010:q43.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 43
ce:2010:q43.question:
If the ${BOD}_3$ of a wastewater sample is 75mg/L and reaction rate constant k
(base e) is 0.345 per day, the amount of BOD remaining in the given sample after
10 days is

primary.subtopicLabel: Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
The BOD at any instant is given by,

$$\begin{aligned} L_{t} &=L\left [ 1-e^{-kt} \right ] \\ \Rightarrow \; \;75&=L\left [ 1-e^{-0.345} \right ] \\ \Rightarrow \; \; L&=\frac{75}{1-0.355} \\ \Rightarrow \; \; L &=116.32\: mg/l \end{aligned}$$

BOD after 10 days,

$$\begin{aligned} L_{10} &=L\left [ 1-e^{-0.345\times 10} \right ] \\ &=116.32\times 0.968 \\ &=112.63\: mg/l \end{aligned}$$

Amount of BOD remaining =$L-L_{0}$

$$\begin{aligned} &=116.32-112.63 \\ &=3.69\: mg/l \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ce:2010:q44.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 44
ce:2010:q44.question:
Consider the following statements in the context of geometric design of roads.
I : A simple parabolic curve is an acceptable shape for summit curves
II : Comfort to passengers is an important consideration in the design of summit curves.
The correct otption evaluating the above statements and their relationship is
options: I is true, II is false
I is true, II is true, and II is the correct reason for I
I is true, II is true, and II is NOT the correct reason for I
I is false, II is true

primary.subtopicLabel: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Geometric Design of Highway and Planning
detailed_solution.markdown:
When fast moving vehicle travels along a summit

curve the centrifugal force will act upwards

against gravity and hence a part of the pressure

on the tyres and spring of the vehicle suspensions

is relieved. So there is no problem of discomfort

to passengers on Summit curves. The only

problem is designing summit curves is to provide

adequate sight distances.

Circular summit curve is ideal curve as the sight

distance available throughout the length of circular >

curve is constant. The deviation angles in vertical

curves of highways are very small and so between

the same tangent points, a simple parabola is

nearly congruent with a circular arc; also a

parabola is very easy for arithmetical manipulation

for computing ordinates. Thus, in actual practice

a simple parabolic curve is used as a summit

curve instead of the circular arc.

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2010:q45.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 45
ce:2010:q45.question:
The design speed for a two-lane road is 80 km/h. When a design vehicle with a
wheelbase of 6.6 m is negotiating a horizontal curve on that road, the off-tracking
is measured as 0.096 m. The required widening of carriageway of the two-lane
road on the curve is approximately

primary.subtopicLabel: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Geometric Design of Highway and Planning
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \text { Off-tracking, } \frac{l^{2}}{2 R} &=0.096 \mathrm{m} \\ \Rightarrow\quad R &=\frac{(6.6)^{2}}{2 \times 0.096}=226.875 \mathrm{m} \\ \text { Extra widening, } E_{w} &=n \times \frac{l^{2}}{2 R}+\frac{V}{9.5 \sqrt{R}} \\ &=2 \times 0.096+\frac{80}{9.5 \sqrt{226.875}} \\ &=0.192+0.56=0.752 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ce:2010:q47.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 47
ce:2010:q47.question:
A bench mark has been established at the soffit of an ornamental arch at the
known elevation of 100.0 m above mean sea level. The back sight used to establish
height of instrument is a inverted staffreading of 2.105m. A forward sight reading
with normally held staff of 1.105m is taken on a recently constructed plinth. The
elevation of the plinth is

detailed_solution.concept: Geomatics Engineering - Levelling and Contouring
detailed_solution.markdown:
Height of instrument =BM + Back sight

since, the staff is inverted, the back sight will be negative.

$\therefore$ Height of instrument

$=100+(-2.105)=97.897 m$

Elevation of plinth = Height of instrument-Fore sight

$=97.895-1.105=96.790 \mathrm{m}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2010:q48.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 48
ce:2010:q48.question:
Ion concentrations obtained for a groundwater sample (having pH=8.1) are given below.

Total hardness (mg/L as $CaCO_3$) present in the above water sample is

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Quality Characteristics of Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
Total hardness

$$\begin{aligned} &=\left[\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}\right] \times \frac{\mathrm{eq} \cdot \mathrm{wt} . \text { of } \mathrm{CaCO}_{3}}{\mathrm{eq} \cdot \mathrm{wt} \cdot \mathrm{of} \mathrm{Mg}^{2+}} \\ &\qquad +\left[\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}\right] \times \frac{\mathrm{eq} . \mathrm{wt} . \text { of } \mathrm{CaCO}_{3}}{\text { eq. wh. of } \mathrm{Ca}^{2+}} \\ &=6 \times \frac{50}{12}+100 \times \frac{50}{20}=275 \mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{L} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ce:2010:q49.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 49
ce:2010:q49.question:
Ion concentrations obtained for a groundwater sample (having pH=8.1) are given below.

Carbonate hardness (mg/L as $CaCO_3$) present in the above water sample is

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Quality Characteristics of Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
Total alkalinity in water consists of alkalinity caused by $\mathrm{CO}_{3}^{2-}, \mathrm{HCO}_{3}\text{ and }\mathrm{OH}^{-}.$

A little negative

alkalinity is also caused by $\mathrm{H}^{+}$

$$\begin{aligned} \therefore \text { Total Alkalinity } &=\left[\mathrm{HCO}_{3}^{-}\right] \times \frac{\mathrm{Eq} \cdot \mathrm{wt} . \text { of } \mathrm{CaCO}_{3}}{\mathrm{Eq}, \mathrm{wt} . \text { of } \mathrm{HCO}_{3}^{-}} \\ &=250 \times \frac{50}{61}=205 \mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{L} \end{aligned}$$

Carbonate hardness is equal to the total hardness or alkalinity, whichever is less. The carbonate hardness of the sample will be $205 \mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{L}$

$\therefore$ Non-carbonate hardness

= Total hardness - carbonate hardness

$=275-205=70 \mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{L}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2010:q50.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 50
ce:2010:q50.question:
The moisture holding capacity of the soil in a 100 hectare farm is 18cm/m. the field is to be irrigated when 50 percent of the available moisture in the root zone is depleted. The irrigation water is to be supplied by a pump working for 10hours a day, and water application efficiency is 75%. Details of crops planned for cultivation are as follows:

The capacity of irrigation system to irrigate crop 'X' in 36 hectares is

detailed_solution.concept: Irrigation engineering - Crop Water Requirements
detailed_solution.markdown:
Moisture holding capacity of soil =18cm / m

Root zone depth of crop X=1.0 m M

Moisture holding capacity of soil for crop

$X=18 \times 1=18 \mathrm{cm}$

Allowable depletion of moisture

$=\frac{50}{100} \times 18=9 \mathrm{cm}$

Consumptive use of water for crop

$X=0.5 \mathrm{cm} / \text { day }$

$\therefore$ Frequency of irrigation $=\frac{9}{0.5}=18\text{days}$

Thus 9 cm depth of water is to be applied to the

crop X in the next 18 days.

Irrigation requirement

$=\frac{\text { Net water depth }}{\text { Water application efficiency }}$

$=\frac{9}{0.75}=12 \mathrm{cm}$

Quantity of water required

$\therefore \quad$ Discharge through pump

$=\frac{43200}{18 \times 10 \times 60 \times 60} \times 10^{3}\text{ litres/sec}$

$=66.67 \text{ litres/sec }\simeq 67 \quad\text{ litres/sec}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2010:q52.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 52
ce:2010:q52.question:
A doubly reinforced rectangular concrete beam has a width of 300mm and an effective depth of 500mm. the beam is reinforced with 2200$mm^2$ of steel in tension and 628$mm^2$ of steel in compression. The effective cover for compression steel is 50mm. Assume that both tension and compression steel yield. The grades of concrete and steel used are M20 and Fe250 respectively. The stress lock parameters (rounded off to first two decimal places) for concrete shall be as per IS 456:200.

The depth of neutral axis is

detailed_solution.concept: RCC Structures - Footing, Columns, Beams and Slabs
detailed_solution.markdown:
The resultant compressive force in the concrete is given by,

$C_{u c}=0.36 \mathrm{f}_{c k} b x_{u}$

The resultant compressive force in the compression steel is given by,

$C_{u s}=\left(f_{s c}-0.45 f_{c k}\right) A_{s c}$

The resultant tensile force in the tensile steel is given by,

$T_{u}=0.87 \mathrm{f} / \mathrm{A}_{s t}$

we know that,

$$\begin{array}{c} C_{u c}+C_{u s}=T_{u} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0.36 f_{c k} b x_{u}+\left(f_{s c}-0.45 f_{c k}\right) A_{s c} =0.87 f_{r} A_{s t} \\ \Rightarrow \quad x_{u}=\frac{0.87 f_{y} A_{s t}-\left(f_{s c}-0.45 f_{c k}\right) A_{s c}}{0.36 f_{\alpha} b} \end{array}$$

Assuming $f_{s c}=0.87 f_{y}$

$$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad x_{u}&=\frac{-(0.87 \times 250-0.45 \times 20) \times 628}{0.36 \times 20 \times 300} \\ \Rightarrow \quad x_{u}&=160.91 \mathrm{mm} \\ \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{But }x_{u, \max }&=0.53 d\text{ for }\mathrm{Fe} 250 \\ \therefore \quad x_{u, \max }&=0.53 \times 500=265 \mathrm{mm} \\ x_{u}& \lt x_{u, \max } ,\text{ hence the assumption}\\ f_{s c}&=0.87 \mathrm{f}_{y} \text{ is justified.} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ce:2010:q53.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 53
ce:2010:q53.question:
A doubly reinforced rectangular concrete beam has a width of 300mm and an effective depth of 500mm. the beam is reinforced with 2200$mm^2$ of steel in tension and 628$mm^2$ of steel in compression. The effective cover for compression steel is 50mm. Assume that both tension and compression steel yield. The grades of concrete and steel used are M20 and Fe250 respectively. The moment of resistance of the section is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Moment of resistance $M_{u}$ is given by.

$$\begin{aligned} M_{u}=& C_{u c}\left(d-0.42 x_{u}\right)+C_{u s}(d-d) \\ =& 0.36 f_{c k} b r_{u}\left(d-0.42 x_{U}\right) \\ &+\left(f_{s c}-0.45 f_{c k}\right) A_{s c}(d-d) \\ =& 0.36 \times 20 \times 300 \times 160.91 \\ &(500-0.42 \times 160.91) \\ &+(0.87 \times 250-0.45 \times 20) \\ & \times 628(500-50) \\ =& 209215652.1 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{kN}-\mathrm{m} \\ =& 209.21 \mathrm{kN}-\mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

ce:2010:q55.title: GATE CE 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 55
